newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude prices sharply higher with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude prices sharply higher with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices rose sharply Thursday, amid lackluster local trade and a jump in New York energy futures prices, traders said.
Sales of Alaska North Slope (ANs) crude -- the West Coast regional benchmark -- remained unchanged.
Key seller BP continued to offer at $1.85 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI)
Discounts for ANS remained $2.16 a barrel under WTI. With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude rose to $17.77/17.94 a barrel.
Light Line 63 crude also rose with spot WTI, while its discount remained steady at minus $3.05 a barrel, and its price over Buena Vista stood unchanged at 90 cents to $1.00.
Meanwhile, Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- rose after major oil companies increased postings late Thursday.
